_purpose: Machine-checkable contract for the weekly content dashboard. This file exists because the dashboard lost 72% of its content between 2026-05-21 (216KB) and 2026-06-22 (60KB), losing features one at a time across rebuilds, and nobody noticed until the artifacts were diffed side by side. Prose rules did not prevent that; three separate rule files each claimed to be canonical and each described a different page. A rebuild is now PASS/FAIL against this manifest instead of against anyone's memory.
_how_to_use: After building a dashboard, run: python scripts/validate_dashboard.py <built.html>. Exit 0 = every required element present. Exit 1 = something regressed; the output names exactly what. Never publish a dashboard that has not passed. Never build by copying last week's output (see _build_rule).
_build_rule: BUILD FROM THE TEMPLATE, NEVER FROM LAST WEEK'S OUTPUT. The scheduled task previously said to replicate the most recent production-calendar.html. That is the root cause of the decay: copying an output means any feature that dropped once is gone permanently, and each week's loss compounds. Start from templates/main-dashboard-template.html, fill it with this week's data, then validate.
_provenance: Reconciled 2026-08-13 from three conflicting specs (weekly-dashboard-rules.md, weekly-calendar-rules.md, content-calendar/references/dashboard-architecture.md) against the REAL published artifacts in online-content/dashboards/weekly-calendars/. Where the specs disagreed, the built artifact won, because that is the page Graeham actually opens. High-water mark used as the baseline: 2026-05-21 (216KB).

page._h1_note: Chosen by Graeham 2026-08-13 as the self-explanatory title. The old weekly-calendar-rules.md forbade the words 'Weekly Calendar' in the title while the canonical filename was production-calendar.html; that contradiction is retired. The FILENAME stays production-calendar.html for URL continuity.

_tabs_note: These five are what the real artifacts have shipped since 2026-05-21. weekly-dashboard-rules.md said Research/Diagram/Calendar/Video/Blog; weekly-calendar-rules.md said Research/Diagram/Content/Video Content/Blog Content. The built page is a hybrid of both, and it is the authority.

content_minimums._note: Both tabs shipped 'All 5 Topics' in every real artifact. Fewer than 5 means the generation pass dropped output, which is the failure mode this whole manifest exists to catch.
content_minimums._size_note: The high-water mark was 216KB (2026-05-21) and the last build was 60KB. A dashboard under 150KB is almost certainly missing content even if every signature above happens to match. This is a blunt instrument on purpose: it catches silent truncation that signature checks miss.

brand._rule: Brand values live ONLY in ../../shared-references/identity.json. validate_dashboard.py loads required_dre and the forbidden list from there at runtime; nothing is hardcoded here so the repo's blocked-DRE tripwire stays clean.
